borrowed: Graph theory, where a path is a sequence of edges. Here it always runs top to bottom through the levels, never sideways.
definition: A path is one top-to-bottom line through the graph, from a node nothing constrains to a node nothing rests on.
name: path

rejected.because: Lineage already names the parent chain the graph layer owns, which is a different thing from a top-to-bottom line.
rejected.name: lineage

rejected.because: A chain says the links are equal, and a path descends through ordered levels.
rejected.name: chain

rejected.because: A route is a way through code, which is the sense this word was taken back from; the commit command is called a command.
rejected.name: route
